classification.difficultyReason: Match six differently oriented triangles using three congruence tests and corresponding vertex order.

content.prompt: From the six triangles drawn, name three pairs of congruent triangles. Give reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above the horizontal base CB. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: AC = 1.5 cm; AB = 2.5 cm; CB = 3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All measurements are permanent givens; no pairing is shown.

spec.description: Right triangle DEF with DF vertical, FE horizontal and a right-angle square at F.
spec.mathematics: DE = 5 cm; FE = 3.5 cm; angle DFE = 90 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle GHJ with G above horizontal JH and the given angle inside J.
spec.mathematics: JG = 3.5 cm; JH = 5 cm; angle GJH = 35 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle KLM with horizontal MK above L and the given angle inside M.
spec.mathematics: MK = 5 cm; ML = 3.5 cm; angle KML = 35 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle NOP with horizontal PO and N above and slightly right of O.
spec.mathematics: PN = 3 cm; NO = 1.5 cm; PO = 2.5 cm.

spec.description: Right triangle QRS with SQ horizontal, QR vertical and a right-angle square at Q.
spec.mathematics: SQ = 3.5 cm; SR = 5 cm; angle SQR = 90 degrees.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle OPN$ (SSS).

$\triangle DEF\equiv\triangle RSQ$ (RHS).

$\triangle GHJ\equiv\triangle LKM$ (SAS).
answer.worked:
$AB=OP=2.5\text{ cm}$, $BC=PN=3\text{ cm}$ and $CA=NO=1.5\text{ cm}$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle OPN$ (SSS).

$\angle DFE=\angle RQS=90^\circ$, the hypotenuses satisfy $DE=RS=5\text{ cm}$, and $EF=SQ=3.5\text{ cm}$. Therefore $\triangle DEF\equiv\triangle RSQ$ (RHS).

$GJ=LM=3.5\text{ cm}$, $HJ=KM=5\text{ cm}$ and the included angles satisfy $\angle GJH=\angle LMK=35^\circ$. Therefore $\triangle GHJ\equiv\triangle LKM$ (SAS).
